Order rows and columns

Source: R/order.R
calor_order.Rd

Sort the heatmap without drawing a tree. Ordering is resolved when the plot is built, so it composes with calor_dendro(): a dendrogram wins for the axis it clusters.

Usage

calor_order(rows = NULL, cols = NULL, decreasing = TRUE)

Arguments

rows, cols

How to order. One of:

  • a statistic name: "mean", "sum", "max", "min", "var", "sd", "median";

  • "cluster": hierarchical-clustering leaf order, no tree drawn;

  • "memo": the oncoprint sort. Items are ordered so that those with a value in the first row/column come first, then the second, and so on. Combine with "sum" on the other axis for a classic oncoprint;

  • a name: order rows by the values in that column, or columns by the values in that row;

  • a character vector of names or an integer vector: an explicit order;

  • a function taking the matrix and returning an order. NULL leaves the axis as is.

decreasing

Sort statistics from largest to smallest.

Value

An object to add to a ggcalor() plot with +.

Examples

m <- matrix(rnorm(80), 10, 8, dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:10), paste0("s", 1:8)))
ggcalor(m) + calor_order(rows = "mean", cols = "cluster")

ggcalor(m) + calor_order(rows = "s1")
